a1.cap: Expose GET /api/books?page=0&size=20&sort=title,asc returning one page of books as lightweight DTOs, with the page size capped at 100 so clients can't request huge pages.
a1.say: Expose GET /api/books?page equals 0 and size equals 20 and sort equals title, asc returning one page of books as lightweight DTOs, with the page size capped at 100 so clients can't request huge pages.

lines: Expose GET /api/books?page=0&size=20&sort=title,asc returning one page of books as lightweight DTOs, with the page size capped at 100 so clients can't request huge pages.

a1.cap: Declaring a Pageable parameter lets Spring parse page, size and sort from the query string. The repository returns a Page, and map converts each entity into a DTO so you never expose JPA entities directly.
@PageableDefault sets sensible defaults; the global spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size property caps abuse.
a1.say: at Pageable Default sets sensible defaults; the global spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size property caps abuse.

a1.cap: A small DTO record controls exactly which fields leave the API.
Constructor injection: Spring passes the repository in, and the field can be final.
Defaults apply when the client sends no paging parameters: 20 items sorted by title.
findAll(pageable) runs a LIMIT/OFFSET query plus a count query.
a1.say: find All(pageable) runs a LIMIT/OFFSET query plus a count query.

a1.cap: Page.map converts each entity to a DTO while keeping the paging metadata.
This property caps page sizes globally, so size=10000 is silently reduced to 100.
a1.say: This property caps page sizes globally, so size equals 10000 is silently reduced to 100.
